name_en: Dagojiru — hand-torn wheat dumplings simmered in a root-vegetable miso soup
summary_ja: 小麦粉の生地を手で延ばしちぎった団子を、里芋やごぼうなど季節の野菜と味噌や醤油で煮込んだ汁もの。「だご」は熊本弁でだんごの意味で、農作業の合間の食事として親しまれてきたという。
summary_en: Wheat-flour dough is torn by hand into dumplings and simmered with seasonal root vegetables in a miso or soy broth. "Dago" is Kumamoto dialect for dumpling, and the dish is said to have long fed farmers between fieldwork.

name_en: Tsubonjiru — a clear soy-seasoned soup of chicken, kamaboko, and root vegetables served in odd numbers
summary_ja: 鶏肉やかまぼこ、里芋やごぼうなど根菜を小さく刻み、いりこ出汁と醤油で仕立てた汁もの。人吉球磨地域の秋祭りの会席膳が起源とされ、具材は7種や9種など奇数で揃えるならわしがあるという。
summary_en: Chicken, kamaboko, and root vegetables like taro and burdock are cut small and simmered in a soy-seasoned sardine broth. Said to originate in autumn-festival banquet trays of the Hitoyoshi-Kuma area, its ingredients are traditionally kept to an odd number.
